name: Fan Tuan (Taiwanese Stuffed Rice Roll)

ingredients.name: youtiao, cut to about 6 inches long
neutral oil, such as vegetable, divided

instructions.primary_message: Place long-grain glutinous rice and purple rice in a large bowl and cover by 2 inches of cool water. Using your hands, vigorously swish rice until water turns cloudy, about 30 seconds. Using a fine-mesh strainer, drain rice, discarding the cloudy soaking water. Refill bowl with cool water and repeat rinsing and draining process until water runs clear.
Return washed rice to large bowl and cover with room temperature water. Soak rice, uncovered, for at least 4 hours and up to 12 hours in the refrigerator.

Using a fine-mesh strainer, drain rice. Line a bamboo steamer with wet cheesecloth. Transfer rice to cheesecloth-lined bamboo steamer and spread in an even layer. Using your finger, poke evenly spaced holes into the rice mound; this will help the rice cook uniformly. Fold the flaps of the cheesecloth over the rice, and cover. (Cheesecloth doesn’t have to fully cover rice; the folding ensures the flaps don’t sit in the water. See notes for instructions on preparing the rice if you don’t have a bamboo steamer.)

Fill a large wok with 2 inches water, and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Cover bamboo steamer basket and lower it into the wok. Steam until rice is al dente and shiny, about 30 minutes, replenishing the bottom of the wok with boiling water if needed.
Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 350ºF (180ºC).
Rinse the pickled mustard greens under cold running water. Squeeze out excess water, and pat dry with paper towels. Mince and set aside for later.
Cut the crullers in half lengthwise and toast in the oven on a 9- by 13- inch rimmed baking sheet until dark golden brown, 5 to 8 minutes. (They should be very crispy but not burnt.)

In a medium nonstick pan, heat 1 teaspoon vegetable oil over low until just shimmering. Add the minced pickled mustard greens, diced bean curd, and sugar and cook, stirring constantly, until sugar has dissolved and the greens are withered and dried out, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a plate and set aside for later.
In a small bowl, whisk eggs, salt, and 1 tablespoon water until smooth. Using a fine-mesh sieve, strain mixture into a clean bowl.

In a medium nonstick skillet, add remaining 1/2 teaspoon oil over medium-low heat until just shimmering. When the pan is hot, pour in egg mixture and tilt pan so the egg forms a thin and even film. Immediately cover the pan with a lid and cook until eggs are set, about 1 minute. Turn off heat, and wait until egg completely solidifies, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Remove lid and, when egg is cool enough to handle, use your fingers or chopsticks gently peel it off the frying pan and place it on a cutting board. Roll egg up tightly, and cut it crosswise into 1/4 inch- thick strips.

To Assemble: Fold a clean kitchen towel so it forms a rectangle roughly 7 inches by 6 inches. Arrange towel on kitchen counter with the long sides parallel to the counter edge. Cover towel completely with plastic wrap.

Dip a spoon in water and use it to spread about 1/4 (about 6 ounces; 170g) of the cooked rice evenly across plastic wrap, leaving a 1/2-inch border on all sides. The long side of the rectangle should still be facing you.

Sprinkle a line of the egg strips down the length of the rice rectangle, add the diced bean curd and mustard greens on top, and then finally a chunk of the fried cruller lined up vertically on top of everything.
Lift up towel and plastic wrap to roll rice over the filling, using your hands to gently squeeze and shape the sticky rice into an oblong rice roll.
Repeat for remaining rice rolls. Take it to go, or unwrap the plastic and enjoy immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: fan tuan, how to make fan tuan

description: Originally an obscure breakfast item enjoyed mainly by the Chinese refugees who introduced it, fan tuan—a portable burrito-shaped rice roll typically filled with pork floss and a crispy cruller—has become an everyday staple in Taiwan.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 5 hr.

Optional substitutions: long-grain glutinous rice → sticky rice; purple rice → black glutinous rice or sticky rice

Notes: If you don’t have a bamboo steamer, you can steam the rice in a large pot: Line a colander or fine-mesh sieve with cheesecloth. Transfer rice to cheesecloth-lined colander or fine-mesh sieve and arrange rice as evenly as possible. Using your finger, poke evenly spaced holes into the rice round; this will help the rice cook uniformly. Fold the flaps of the cheesecloth over the rice, and cover.
Fill a large pot with 2 inches water, and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Lower colander or fine-mesh sieve into the pot and cover. Steam until rice is al dente and shiny, about 30 minutes, replenishing the bottom of the wok with boiling water if needed. Proceed with step 5 of the recipe.
author: Clarissa Wei
